feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 3 (0.6 kg, 0.10 m track, y = 0.03 m, kp 2.5, kd 0.4) gave oval progress 0.45 and oscillation 0.309, so the light robot covers the most ground but twitches. Iteration 4 (0.8 kg, same track) gave oscillation 0.181 and progress 0.34, so inertia trades progress for damping. Iteration 5 (y = 0.02 m, 0.8 kg) gave zero line loss on every track, including the slalom, which had 0.25 events at y = 0.03 m. So your row move and the light inertia are compatible on sensing. The oscillation cost is for the controller, and I have lowered kp to 2.2 and raised kd to 0.5. Max_error has stayed at 0.061 to 0.064 m in every iteration, whatever the geometry. Next race: if oscillation is at or below 0.2 and progress is above 0.4, keep this geometry and record max_error as the controller's problem. If oscillation is still above 0.2, I will reduce kp further in the controller, and geometry should not change for that. If progress falls below 0.35 with line loss rising, return the mass to 0.8 kg as in iteration 5, since that is the only geometry that has held the line on the oval.
requested_changes: If oval steering_oscillation stays above 0.2 with mass 0.6 kg and body_length 0.12 m: keep these values, since oscillation is a controller issue here; I will lower kp, and you should not widen the track again (iteration 3 at 0.10 m gave 0.309 and iteration 2 at 0.09 m gave 0.272).
If line_loss_events rise above about 0.25 on the slalom with y = 0.02 m and 0.6 kg: try sensor_size 0.012 at the same positions, as iteration 5 showed zero losses at 0.8 kg with the 16 mm footprint.
If oval progress falls below 0.35 with oscillation at or below 0.2: restore mass 0.8 kg and body_length 0.16 m, since iteration 5 at that inertia gave progress 0.358 with no line loss.
